translation_en: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us; Sulayman narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The womb is a bond from the Most Merciful. Allah said: Whoever maintains ties with you, I will maintain ties with him; and whoever severs you, I will sever ties with him.”

Said ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us; Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, saying: Muawiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid informed me, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Urwah, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The womb is a branch of kinship. Whoever maintains it, I will maintain ties with him; whoever severs it, I will sever ties with him.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-Amash, al-Hasan ibn Amr, and Fitr, from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn Amr. Sufyan said: Al-Amash did not attribute it to the Prophet, but al-Hasan and Fitr did. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The one who truly maintains family ties is not the one who merely reciprocates; rather, the one who truly maintains them is the one who keeps them when his relatives sever them.”

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Hakim ibn Hizam told him: I said, “Messenger of Allah, what about good deeds I used to do in the pre-Islamic age, such as maintaining ties, freeing slaves, and giving charity? Will I be rewarded for them?” Hakim said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, replied: “You accepted Islam along with the good you had done before.” It is also reported from Abu al-Yaman with the wording “I used to seek goodness.” Mamar, Salih, and Ibn al-Musafir also reported that wording. Ibn Ishaq said that seeking goodness means doing righteous deeds; Hisham also reported it from his father.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham, from Urwah, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “You kiss children, but we do not kiss them.” The Prophet said: “What can I do for you if Allah has removed mercy from your heart?”

Al-Hakam ibn Nafi informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Said ibn al-Musayyab informed us that Abu Hurairah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Allah made mercy one hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine parts with Himself and sent down one part to earth. By that one part, creation shows mercy to one another, so much so that a mare lifts her hoof from her foal for fear of hurting it.”

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me: I heard Sahl ibn Sad, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “I and the caretaker of an orphan will be in Paradise like this.” He held up his index and middle fingers.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us; Malik narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The one who strives to support a widow and a poor person is like a fighter in the way of Allah”—and I think he said, al-Qanabi was uncertain—“like one who stands in prayer without tiring and one who fasts without breaking his fast.”

Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Zakariyya narrated to us, from Amir, who said: I heard him say: I heard al-Numan ibn Bashir say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “You see the believers in their mutual mercy, love, and compassion as one body: when one part suffers, the rest of the body responds with sleeplessness and fever.”

Abu al-Walid narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whenever a Muslim plants a plant and a person or an animal eats from it, it is charity for him.”

Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Wahb narrated to me: I heard Jarir ibn Abdullah report from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.”

Ismail ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Said, who said: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad informed me, from Amrah, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Gabriel continued advising me to treat the neighbor well until I thought he would make him an heir.”

Muhammad ibn Minhal narrated to us; Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us; Umar ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Gabriel continued advising me to treat the neighbor well until I thought he would make him an heir.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us; Said—the gravedigger—narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say: “Muslim women, let no neighbor look down on a gift from her neighbor, even if it is a sheep's hoof.”

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.”

Ali ibn Ayyash narrated to us; Abu Ghassan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Every good deed is charity.”

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik: A Bedouin urinated in the mosque, and the people rose to stop him. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Do not interrupt him.” Then he called for a bucket of water and poured it over the spot.

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Wail, who said: I heard Masruq say: Abdullah ibn Amr said so. Qutaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Masruq, who said: We visited Abdullah ibn Amr when he arrived in Kufa with Muawiyah. He mentioned the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, saying: “He was not obscene or vulgar.” He also said the Messenger of Allah said: “The best of you are those with the best character.”

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us; Abu Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Musa ibn Uqbah informed me, from Nafi, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “When Allah loves a servant, He calls Gabriel: ‘Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.’ Gabriel loves him, then calls out to the inhabitants of Heaven: ‘Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.’ The inhabitants of Heaven love him, and then acceptance of him is placed among the people of earth.”

Adam narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “No one will find the sweetness of faith until he loves a person only for Allah's sake, until being thrown into the Fire is dearer to him than returning to disbelief after Allah saved him from it, and until Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than anything else.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: I heard Abu Wail relate from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Insulting a Muslim is wickedness, and fighting him is disbelief.” Ghundar also reported it from Shu'bah.

Abu Mamar narrated to us; Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah. Yahya ibn Yamar narrated to me that Abu al-Aswad al-Dili told him, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “If a man accuses another of wickedness or disbelief, it returns upon him if the other person is not as he said.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us; Ali ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Qilabah, that Thabit ibn al-Dahhak, one of the companions who pledged allegiance beneath the tree, told him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever swears by a religion other than Islam is as he said. A human being cannot make a vow concerning what he does not possess. Whoever kills himself with something in this world will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever curses a believer is like one who kills him, and whoever accuses a believer of disbelief is like one who kills him.”

Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us, saying: Adi ibn Thabit narrated to me: I heard Sulayman ibn Surad, a man from among the Prophet's companions, say: Two men insulted each other in the Prophet's presence. One of them became angry, and his anger grew until his face swelled and changed color. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I know a phrase which, if he said it, would make what he is feeling go away.” A man went to him, told him what the Prophet had said, and said: “Seek refuge in Allah from Satan.” He replied: “Do you think there is something wrong with me? Am I mad? Go away.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Humayd, who said: Anas said: Ubadah ibn al-Samit narrated to me: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, went out to tell the people about the Night of Decree, but two Muslim men argued. The Prophet said: “I came out to tell you, but so-and-so and so-and-so argued, and it was taken away. Perhaps that is better for you. Seek it on the ninth, seventh, and fifth [of the last ten nights].”

Qabisah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Usayd al-Saidi, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The best homes of the Ansar are those of Banu al-Najjar.”

Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Hammam, who said: We were with Hudhayfah when it was said to him: “A man attributes a report to Uthman.” Hudhayfah said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “A talebearer will not enter Paradise.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhib narrated to us, from al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever does not give up false speech, acting upon it, and ignorant conduct, Allah has no need of him giving up his food and drink.” Ahmad said: A man helped me understand its chain of transmission.

Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “On the Day of Resurrection, you will find the worst of people before Allah to be the two-faced person, who approaches these people with one face and those people with another.”

Bishr ibn Muhammad informed us; Abdullah informed us; Mamar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false kind of speech. Do not seek out people's faults, do not spy, do not envy one another, do not turn away from one another, do not hate one another, and be servants of Allah as brothers.”
